title: PlanRAG: A Plan-then-Retrieval Augmented Generation for Generative Large Language Models as Decision Makers

analysis.tldr: PlanRAG makes an explicit decision plan the upstream controller for iterative data retrieval, rather than letting retrieval proceed as an unstructured sequence of searches.
analysis.problem: Decision-making questions can require multiple dependent data analyses, while a one-shot or weakly structured retrieval loop does not encode what information should be acquired next.
analysis.core_idea: Generate a plan for the decision task first, then derive retrieval/data-analysis queries conditioned on that plan and iterate toward the answer.
analysis.agent_loop: Plan → formulate data query → retrieve/analyze → update reasoning → repeat → decide
analysis.retrieval_design: Retrieval is driven by an explicit high-level plan and is used to acquire database evidence needed for decision QA rather than only retrieving semantically similar passages.
analysis.evidence: The paper reports a new Decision QA benchmark (DQA) and abstract-level gains over an iterative RAG baseline in two scenarios; the bootstrap curator has not yet re-checked the full experimental tables.
analysis.why_it_matters: It is an early clean example of moving control from a fixed RAG pipeline into an explicit retrieval plan, making planning itself part of the retrieval abstraction.
limitations: The evaluation is centered on a specialized Decision QA setting.
The bootstrap note has not yet been upgraded from abstract/metadata review to full-paper verification.
